chunks: I have seen the companions of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), so I do not see anyone among you resembling them!

They would begin the day with disheveled hair and dust-covered faces, having spent the night in prostration and standing (in prayer). They would alternate between their foreheads and their cheeks, and stand firm on the coals from the remembrance of their return (to God)!
It was as if between their eyes were the knees of goats due to the length of their prostration!

When Allah was mentioned, their eyes would flow with tears until they soaked their shirt collars, and they would sway as trees sway on the day of a stormy wind, out of fear of punishment and hope for reward!

key_terms.رُكَبَ الْمِعْزَى: knees of goats (a simile for the swelling of the eyes/cheeks from long prostration)
key_terms.سُجَّدًا وَقِيَامًا: prostrating and standing (referring to night prayer)
key_terms.شُعْثًا غُبْرًا: disheveled and dust-covered (indicating hardship and lack of worldly concern)
key_terms.يُرَاوِحُونَ: they alternate or move back and forth

ai.seo_question: How did the companions of the Prophet demonstrate their devotion through prayer and humility?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) vividly portrays the asceticism and spiritual intensity of the Prophet's companions, whose foreheads bore the marks of prolonged prostration and whose bodies trembled like trees in a storm from awe and hope. This description, found in the 'Admonishing his companions' chapter, serves as a benchmark for true piety, contrasting their raw, embodied devotion with later generations. The imagery underscores the Shia emphasis on *khushu'* (humility) and the physical manifestation of inner faith through consistent night prayers (*Tahajjud*) and remembrance of death (*Mawt*).

en.sayed-ali-raza: I have seen the companions of the Prophet but I do not find anyone resembling them.

They began the day with dust on the hair and face (in hardship of life) and passed the night in prostration and standing in prayers. Sometimes they put down their foreheads and sometimes their cheeks. With the recollection of their resurrection it seemed as though they stood on live coal.
It seemed that in between their eyes there were signs like knees of goats, resulting from long prostrations.
When Allāh was mentioned their eyes flowed freely till their shirt collars were drenched. They trembled for fear of punishment and hope of reward as the tree trembles on the day of stormy wind.
